statement: Increment A adds no runtime allocation, lease, or payload: there is no prepared store, no worker-local cache, and no lease table in this increment. The produced path's memory behavior is unchanged (src diff empty). These are the memory laws increments B/C must satisfy when the surface exists, recorded now as the design posture:

memory_laws_for_B_C.immutable_leases: prepared payloads are immutable and shared; leases never expose public mutable aliasing (CLAUDE.md); consumers materialize independent ordinary objects BEFORE leases close (designs/02:103-104)
memory_laws_for_B_C.per_consumer_copies: wherever the produced path defensively copies (network.weights from lengths, Topology.py:284), the prepared path hands each consumer its own copy
memory_laws_for_B_C.budget_respect: prepared payloads count against execution.memory_limit_bytes / workspace_limit_bytes like every other retained artifact; PP09 (small budget, many distinct roots, eviction with live leases) is the C-increment acceptance fixture
memory_laws_for_B_C.no_pointer_transport: GDALDataset/GEOS/STRtree pointers and open native handles are never transported across processes (designs/02:94-95); restored geometries are rebuilt bytes, derived sindex rebuilt per consumer (fixture-proven query parity)
memory_laws_for_B_C.measurement_duty: prepared_memory.json gains actual caps/lease measurements in B (worker-local) and C (run-wide): payload sizes for the admitted cohort shapes, lease table overhead, eviction behavior
